extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners / counsel, communications professionals, advertisers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical principles and methods a public-relations counsel should use to analyze problems, select media, create news, appeal to human instincts, mobilize groups/leaders, and ethically modify public opinion or behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze the client’s problem and objective
rubrics_metrics.description: First he must analyze his client’s problem and his client’s objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The counsel should understand what the client aims to accomplish before any outreach or message-design begins; this analysis is the foundation for selecting appeals, media and tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze the public to be reached (segmentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: He must analyze the public he is trying to reach ... by that section or those sections of the public which must be reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualize oneself as member of multiple relevant publics (manufacturer, retailer, importer, worker, politician) and further subdivide (geography, age, education, language, interest groups) to identify the appeals that will influence as many sections as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devise a plan of action and determine organs of distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: He must devise a plan of action for the client to follow and determine the methods and the organs of distribution available for reaching his public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate channels (press, moving pictures, lecture, advertising, direct mail, stage, word of mouth, pulpit, schoolroom, legislative chamber) based on audience and goals; align tactics to the channel's strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate interaction between client message and public reception
rubrics_metrics.description: Finally he must try to estimate the interaction between the public he seeks to reach and his client. How will his client’s case strike the public mind?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predict how the public will respond to the message, considering prevailing attitudes, stereotypes, and competing interests; test feasibility of intended appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take changed conditions into account
rubrics_metrics.description: Changed conditions can make possible modifications in the public point of view ... they must be taken into consideration by the public relations counsel in his work if they concern in the slightest degree his particular public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust strategy for technological, social or economic shifts (examples: radio, airplane, automobile, national prohibition) because these alter public viewpoints and channels of influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create news — lift startling facts and develop ideas into events
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel, therefore, is a creator of news ... He must lift startling facts from his whole subject and present them as news. He must isolate ideas and develop them into events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn client material into newsworthy items that will win placement in competitive news markets; isolate interesting facts, dramatize them, and present them in a compact, vivid form akin to a headline or cartoon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify and dramatize abstract/factual material for public consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract discussions and heavy facts ... cannot be given to the public until they are simplified and dramatized. The refinements of reason and the shadings of emotion cannot reach a considerable public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert complex analysis into simple, vivid messages (headlines, visual metaphors) so large audiences can understand and respond; use visual/physical signs to embody vague human qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to universal instincts and desires
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal to the instincts and the universal desires is the basic method through which he produces his results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fundamental human instincts — self-preservation (shelter, food, health, insurance), gustatory/sensory appeals, sex-appeal, parental love, curiosity, pugnacity, self-display, etc. — to frame messages that elicit emotional response; choose the instinct(s) most relevant to the audience and objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pugnacity/contest/issue to attract attention
rubrics_metrics.description: It is this element of conflict...which plays an overwhelming part in the psychology of every crowd ... Nothing so easily catches general attention and creates a crowd as a contest of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame issues as contests or battles, stage debates or contests, personify antagonists, and create spectacles to enlist public interest — but recognize dangers of misuse (suppression/oppression). Examples: public health campaigns using 'kill the germs', contests that drive attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use curiosity and wonder to arouse advance interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Curiosity and wonder are continually employed. In Governmental work...the statesman who has an announcement to make is continually exhausting every effort to arouse public interest in advance of the actual announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ 'feelers', suspense, teasers, puzzles and promotions (e.g., 'What is wrong with this picture?') to build anticipation and public attention before an announcement or release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilize self-display and praise to galvanize supporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Very often the public relations counsel utilizes the self-display-elation motive and draws public attention to particular people in groups, in order to give them a greater interest in the work they are espousing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly praise supporters, name rooms/beds after donors, highlight individuals to increase their commitment and mobilize their networks; use honors and visibility as incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage parental-love and tender-emotion appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Parental love and tenderness are continually employed ... The whole flood of post-war charity-drives was keyed to this pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use children, babies, and imagery of care to evoke compassion and charitable action; imagery must be truthful and sensitive to ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work through group leaders and opinion leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: The gregarious instinct ... gives the public relations counsel the opportunity for his most potent work. The group and herd show everywhere the leader ... who is followed more or less implicitly by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and enlist leaders (society leaders, political leaders, clergy, merchants) whose endorsement will bring followers; form cross-sectional committees mirroring community stereotypes to reinforce credibility (example: hotel anniversary committee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment audiences and select leaders accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: After an analysis of his problem the subdivisions must be made. His action depends upon his selective capacity, and the possibility of approach to the leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose leaders representing the specific subdivisions (by geography, age, interest) to mobilize their constituencies; recognize that some leaders influence multiple groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use stereotypes, symbols and visible objects as shorthand
rubrics_metrics.description: Stereotypes or clichés are a great aid ... The public relations counsel sometimes uses the current stereotypes, sometimes combats them and sometimes creates new ones. Visible objects as stereotypes are often used ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ known stereotypes, symbols, emblems and visual cues (flags, instruments, white buildings for cleanliness) to convey complex ideas quickly; also create new catch-phrases or symbols when appropriate (Roosevelt's 'square deal', 'big stick'). Beware of overuse which reduces effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combat harmful stereotypes when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The combating of the stereotype is seen in the battle waged against the American Valuation Plan ... In fighting the plan, its opponents put the word 'American' in quotation marks ... patriotism was definitely removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately challenge misleading or manipulative stereotypes to reframe public perception; use rhetorical devices to question authenticity of an opponent's branding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use habit, imitation, suggestion and play to elicit response
rubrics_metrics.description: The innate tendencies are susceptibility to suggestion, imitation, habit and play ... When a charity committee is advised to institute a street fair to gather money, the committee is recognizing this tendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design recurring events, contests, fairs and playful activities that tap habitual and imitative behaviors to produce predictable public reactions and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the issue easy to pick out amid information overload
rubrics_metrics.description: He must make it easy for the public to pick his issue out of the great mass of material. He must be able to overcome what has been called 'the tendency on the part of public attention to 'flicker' and 'relax.' He must do for the public mind what the newspaper, with its headlines, accomplishes for its readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise, vivid headlines, simple visuals and clear frames so audiences can quickly recognize and retain the issue; structure messages to compete successfully in attention markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat newsworthiness as central — appeal must win placement
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appeal to the instincts can be made so powerful as to secure acceptance in the medium of dissemination in spite of competitive interests, it can be aptly termed news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether an item will be accepted by chosen media amid competition; ensure the angle is inherently interesting and timed to media needs; understand press routines and what editors value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve the press as a purveyor of truthful, accurate, verifiable news
rubrics_metrics.description: It is because he acts as the purveyor of truthful, accurate and verifiable news to the press that the conscientious and successful counsel on public relations is looked upon with favor by the journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain credibility with journalists by providing accurate, verifiable information; be a reliable source of news rather than merely promotional material to foster lasting press relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crystallize obscure public tendencies and create responsive symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps the chief contribution of the public relations counsel ... is his capacity for crystallizing the obscure tendencies of the public mind before they have reached definite expression. His ability to create those symbols to which the public is ready to respond ... are his contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor emergent public moods, identify nascent trends, and invent symbols/phrases/images that make those tendencies actionable and communicable before competitors do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be ethically wary of demagoguery and substitution of words for acts
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one danger in the use of stereotypes by the public relations counsel. That is, by the substitution of words for acts, demagogues in every field of social relationship can take advantage of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying solely on symbolic language without substantive action; maintain ethical standards to prevent manipulation and loss of public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contests, tests and spectacles strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pugnacity would come that technique ... which is continually devising tests and contests ... Nothing so easily catches general attention and creates a crowd as a contest of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design well-judged contests, debates, prize-fights (charity or symbolic), or spectacles to mobilize attendance and involvement; ensure appropriateness and taste to avoid backlash (example: prize fight for charity may be in bad taste).

rubrics_metrics.name: Match the medium’s nature to the message (news vs. opinion)
rubrics_metrics.description: To the newspaper the public relations counsel serves as a purveyor of news. The modern newspaper's primary function is news; editorial opinion is secondary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame submissions to outlets according to what they prize (news outlets want verifiable news, not opinion); tailor format, tone and content to fit the chosen medium's consumption habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider scale of changed conditions (national vs local)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changed conditions can be national or local in their import and significance ... But they must be taken into consideration ... if they concern in the slightest degree his particular public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a contextual change affects audiences nationally or only locally and adapt messaging and tactics accordingly (e.g., local edicts vs. nationwide policy changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use illustrative examples and committees to confer credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The counsel therefore advises the hotel to make a celebration ... and suggests ... an anniversary committee of a body of business men who represent the cream of the city’s merchants ... A committee of nationally known sales-managers is chosen to act as judges ... success is assured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize events or contests with panels or committees of respected figures as a credibility device; publicize their participation to enhance perceived legitimacy.
